title.en: Journey inside the atom: models, atomic number, mass number and valency

text.en: Break a piece of chalk, again and again. Is there a smallest piece? Ancient Indian and Greek thinkers wondered about this, and modern science found that atoms themselves have parts.

The idea of atoms goes back to ancient thinkers in India and Greece, and was developed scientifically by Dalton.
Thomson found the electron and proposed a model with electrons in a positive sphere. Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed a tiny dense nucleus.
Bohr's model puts electrons in fixed orbits or energy levels around the nucleus.
An atom has protons (positive) and neutrons (no charge) in the nucleus and electrons (negative) around it.
The atomic number Z is the number of protons. It identifies the element.
The mass number A is protons plus neutrons.
Electrons fill energy levels in order: at most 2 in the first shell and 8 in the second.
Valency is the combining capacity of an atom and depends on the electrons in the outermost shell.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking electrons are in the nucleus

points.en: Atoms contain protons, neutrons and electrons.
Rutherford discovered the nucleus; Bohr gave energy levels.
Atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons.
